name: org.osgi.service.log
description: OSGi Specification repo for org.osgi.service.log: Java API, specification chapter and TCK
description_good_justification: org.osgi.service.log is part of the OSGi Specification Project, which defines the OSGi specifications: standard Java APIs for modular, service-oriented applications (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). The repository holds the Java API, the specification chapter and the TCK of one specification, as far as it has them; the README describes it (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md).
interact_justification: The README says how to obtain the API (Maven Central, https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/org.osgi/org.osgi.service.log), lists a compatible implementation and gives the feedback channels: mailing lists, Slack (https://osgiwg.slack.com/) and the bi-weekly specification call (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md#contact). Bugs go to https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues; how to contribute is in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md.
contribution_justification: The contribution process (issue, fork, pull request, Eclipse Contributor Agreement, review and merge) is described in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements for acceptable contributions: a signed Eclipse Contributor Agreement (https://www.eclipse.org/legal/eca/), a commit author email that matches the Eclipse account, the copyright and license header and the commit message format (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
floss_license_justification: The project is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/LICENSE), a FLOSS license approved by the OSI (https://opensource.org/license/apache-2-0).
floss_license_osi_justification: The Apache License 2.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative: https://opensource.org/license/apache-2-0.
license_location_justification: The license is in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/LICENSE; notices are in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/NOTICE.
documentation_basics_justification: The user documentation is the specification chapter with its examples, published for every release at https://docs.osgi.org/specification/, together with the Javadoc at https://docs.osgi.org/javadoc/. The README lists the Maven artifact and the compatible implementations (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md).
documentation_interface_justification: The API reference is the Javadoc of each release (https://docs.osgi.org/javadoc/) and the API sections of the specification chapter (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/): every type, method, parameter, return value and exception is specified.
sites_https_justification: All project sites use HTTPS: https://www.osgi.org, https://docs.osgi.org, https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log, https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi and the download site Maven Central (https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/org.osgi/org.osgi.service.log). HTTP requests to www.osgi.org and docs.osgi.org are redirected to HTTPS.
discussion_justification: Discussion happens in GitHub issues and pull requests (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues), which are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone, and on the public mailing list osgi-dev (https://accounts.eclipse.org/mailing-list/osgi-dev, archive https://www.eclipse.org/lists/osgi-dev/), where the minutes of the bi-weekly specification call are posted. The Slack workspace https://osgiwg.slack.com/ is an additional, invitation-based channel.
english_justification: The specification (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/), Javadoc, README and CONTRIBUTING are in English, and bug reports and comments are accepted in English (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues, https://www.eclipse.org/lists/osgi-dev/).
maintained_justification: The OSGi Specification Project is actively maintained: the committers meet in a bi-weekly specification call with agenda and minutes on https://accounts.eclipse.org/mailing-list/osgi-dev, and every specification repository receives its changes through pull requests (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/commits/main). The project passed its Eclipse progress and graduation review in March 2026 (https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/governance).
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public Git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log.
repo_track_justification: Git records every change, its author and its date: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/commits/main.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main through commits and pull requests between releases (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/pulls?q=is%3Apr), and every push to main publishes an interim SNAPSHOT to Sonatype Central snapshots (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml).
repo_distributed_justification: The repository uses Git, a common distributed version control system: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version: the Maven version of org.osgi:org.osgi.service.log (https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/org.osgi/org.osgi.service.log), whose major and minor numbers equal the version of the specification chapter (https://docs.osgi.org/artifacts/).
version_semver_justification: OSGi defines semantic versioning (major.minor.micro) for packages and bundles (https://docs.osgi.org/whitepaper/semantic-versioning/), and the build enforces correct version increases with bnd baselining against the last release (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/spec-build.yml).
version_tags_justification: Each release is identified by a git tag. A release from this repository is created by a tag equal to the Maven version, and the release workflow refuses any other tag (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md#versioning-and-releases). No release has been made from this repository yet, so it has no tags; earlier releases are tagged in the monorepo the history was extracted from: https://github.com/osgi/osgi/tags.
release_notes_justification: Each specification version has a human-readable "Changes" section in its chapter, and each Core and Compendium release summarises its changes in the introduction (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). Each release has an Eclipse release record (https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi).
release_notes_vulns_justification: N/A: no release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability. The Eclipse list of known vulnerabilities has no entry for this project (https://www.eclipse.org/security/known/) and GitHub lists no security advisory for the repository.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in the repository's GitHub issue tracker (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues), as described in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md. Questions can also go to the osgi-dev mailing list (https://accounts.eclipse.org/mailing-list/osgi-dev).
report_tracker_justification: The project uses the GitHub issue tracker for individual issues: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues.
report_responses_justification: Bug reports are answered by the committers in the repository's issue tracker; the full history of reports and responses is public (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues?q=is%3Aissue).
enhancement_responses_justification: The few requests so far were answered or resolved (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed). Larger enhancements are discussed in the public bi-weekly specification call, whose minutes go to osgi-dev (e.g. https://www.eclipse.org/lists/osgi-dev/msg00229.html).
report_archive_justification: GitHub keeps a public, searchable archive of all issues and pull requests (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues?q=is%3Aissue); the mailing list is archived at https://www.eclipse.org/lists/osgi-dev/.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The reporting process is published in the organisation-wide SECURITY.md, which GitHub shows for this repository (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/security/policy; source https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md). It follows the Eclipse Foundation Security Policy (https://www.eclipse.org/security/policy/).
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities can be reported privately by email to the Eclipse Foundation Security Team (security@eclipse-foundation.org), as documented in https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md, or as a confidential issue in the Eclipse vulnerability tracker (https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/vulnerability-reports; see https://www.eclipse.org/security/).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: N/A: no vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months; there is no GitHub security advisory and no Eclipse CVE for this project (https://www.eclipse.org/security/known/). Under the Eclipse process the project security team responds within 2 working days (https://csi.eclipse.dev/security-handbook/vulnerabilities/handling.html).
build_justification: `mvn clean verify` builds the API jar, the specification chapter (HTML and PDF) and the TCK from source (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md#build, https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/pom.xml).
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses Apache Maven (https://maven.apache.org/) with the bnd Maven plugins: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/pom.xml.
build_floss_tools_justification: The whole toolchain is FLOSS: Apache Maven (Apache-2.0, https://maven.apache.org/), bnd (Apache-2.0, https://bnd.bndtools.org/) and OpenJDK.
test_justification: The repository contains the TCK of the specification, an automated JUnit 5 test suite under the Apache-2.0 license (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/tree/main/tck). README and CONTRIBUTING say how to run it, and CI runs it on every push and pull request against a compatible implementation (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/actions/workflows/build.yml).
test_invocation_justification: `mvn clean verify`, the standard Maven lifecycle, builds everything and runs the unit tests and the TCK (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md#build).
test_most_justification: The TCK is the conformance suite of the specification and exercises the specified behaviour of the API (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/tree/main/tck); the Eclipse specification process requires TCK coverage of all verifiable normative statements (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/operations.php#tck). Coverage is not measured yet.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions builds every push to main and every pull request and runs the automated tests, including the TCK (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml, runs: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/actions/workflows/build.yml). The logic is in a central reusable workflow (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/spec-build.yml).
test_policy_justification: The Eclipse Foundation Specification Process requires a TCK for every specification version, covering all parts of the specification (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/#efsp-tck); new normative functionality is added together with its TCK tests.
tests_are_added_justification: The Eclipse Foundation Specification Process requires a TCK for every specification version (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/operations.php#tck). Changes to specified behaviour come with TCK tests in the same pull request (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged).
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy exists in the Eclipse specification process (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/operations.php#tck), but https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md does not yet state that changes must come with TCK tests.
warnings_justification: Every CI build runs CodeQL (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml), bnd baselining (semantic-version check of the API) and maven-enforcer, and a javadoc job in which javadoc errors fail the build (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/spec-build.yml).
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are addressed: CodeQL has no open alerts, a compile of the API with -Xlint:all reports no warnings, and baselining and javadoc errors fail the build (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/actions/workflows/build.yml).
warnings_strict_justification: The Maven build neither enables -Xlint nor fails on compiler warnings, and javadoc doclint is switched off in the parent pom because of legacy HTML in the OSGi sources (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
know_secure_design_justification: The committers design the OSGi security model, the Security Layer of the Core specification (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.core/8.0.0/framework.security.html), and every specification states its security requirements in a Security section (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). They apply least privilege, complete mediation and input validation.
know_common_errors_justification: The committers know the common error classes of Java APIs (missing permission checks, unvalidated input, resource exhaustion, unsafe deserialization) and how to counter them; CodeQL checks every change for them (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml).
crypto_published_justification: N/A: the project produces Java APIs (interfaces, DTOs, annotations and, where a specification defines them, permission classes), specification texts and TCKs. The API implements and calls no cryptography; implementations provide it where a specification needs it (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).

crypto_password_storage_justification: N/A: the API stores no passwords. Where a specification models credentials (User Admin), storing them is up to the implementation (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
crypto_random_justification: N/A: the API generates no cryptographic keys or nonces (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered from Maven Central over HTTPS (https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/org.osgi/org.osgi.service.log); the source is fetched from GitHub over HTTPS or SSH (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
delivery_unsigned_justification: Artifacts and their checksums are retrieved over HTTPS only, and a detached OpenPGP signature is published next to each artifact (https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched publicly known vulnerabilities: the Eclipse list has no entry for this project (https://www.eclipse.org/security/known/) and no Dependabot alert is open. The only alerts so far, in the test dependency assertj-core (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rqfh-9r24-8c9r), were fixed within 7 days.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported for this project. Dependabot security updates are enabled (https://github.com/osgi/.eclipsefdn/blob/main/otterdog/osgi.jsonnet), and the one high-severity alert in a test dependency was fixed within 7 days.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no credentials. CI receives the signing key and the Maven Central token as GitHub organisation secrets that the Eclipse Foundation manages (https://github.com/osgi/.eclipsefdn/blob/main/otterdog/osgi.jsonnet).
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (https://codeql.github.com/) analyses the Java sources on every push to main, on every pull request and weekly: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: The CodeQL Java queries look for common vulnerabilities by CWE (https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/java/): https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL reports no open alerts for this repository (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml). Confirmed findings would be handled under the Eclipse Foundation Security Policy (https://www.eclipse.org/security/policy/).
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push to main, on every pull request and weekly: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is applied to every release yet. The TCK runs the API against a compatible implementation in a live OSGi framework on every build, and some repositories have Jazzer fuzz tests that run as regression tests (example: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.typedevent/pull/65). A scheduled fuzz job is planned.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: N/A: the software is written entirely in Java, a memory-safe language (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/tree/main/api).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Unit tests run under Maven Surefire, which enables Java assertions by default (https://maven.apache.org/surefire/maven-surefire-plugin/test-mojo.html#enableAssertions); the TCK checks the specified run-time behaviour with JUnit and AssertJ assertions (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Defects found by dynamic analysis are fixed promptly and their inputs kept as regression tests; example: the fuzzing findings in TopicPermissionCollection (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.typedevent/pull/65).
achieve_passing_justification: The project is not yet registered on bestpractices.dev (https://www.bestpractices.dev/); this file holds the answers for that registration. Every passing MUST criterion is answered Met or N/A.
dco_justification: Every contributor must have signed the Eclipse Contributor Agreement (https://www.eclipse.org/legal/eca/), which includes the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. The eclipsefdn/eca status check is required on main, so a pull request from an author without ECA cannot be merged (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/handbook/#resources-github).
governance_justification: The project is governed by the Eclipse Foundation Development Process (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/dev_process/), the Eclipse Foundation Specification Process (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/) and the OSGi Working Group charter (https://www.eclipse.org/collaborations/working-groups/osgi/charter/). Committers decide in the open, as described in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md; reviews and releases are on https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/governance.
code_of_conduct_justification: The project follows the Eclipse Foundation Community Code of Conduct (https://www.eclipse.org/org/documents/community-code-of-conduct/), posted as the organisation-wide CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md that GitHub applies to this repository (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
roles_responsibilities_justification: The roles and their duties (contributor, committer, project lead, PMC, specification committee, security team) are defined in the Eclipse Foundation Development Process (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/dev_process/) and the Eclipse Project Handbook (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/handbook/#roles). Who holds which role is listed at https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/who.
access_continuity_justification: The Eclipse Foundation owns the GitHub organisation and manages it as code (https://github.com/osgi/.eclipsefdn/blob/main/otterdog/osgi.jsonnet); write access follows the roles of 2 project leads and 18 committers (https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/who). The Foundation also holds the signing key and the Maven Central credentials as CI secrets, so any committer can release by pushing a tag (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/spec-release.yml), and the project leadership chain can appoint new committers and leads.
bus_factor_justification: Every specification is the work of several parties: the specification editors, the developers of at least one compatible implementation in a separate open source project (listed in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md), and the TCK authors. The full history of this repository, imported from the OSGi monorepo, shows contributors from several organisations (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/graphs/contributors), and the project's committers and project leads can maintain every specification repository with the same build (https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/who).
documentation_roadmap_justification: There is no roadmap for the next twelve months yet. Plans are tracked as GitHub milestones and discussed in the bi-weekly specification call (https://accounts.eclipse.org/mailing-list/osgi-dev).
documentation_architecture_justification: Each specification chapter begins with an introduction that describes the high-level design: essentials, entities and a class and service overview figure (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). How a service fits into the OSGi layers is described in https://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.core/8.0.0/framework.introduction.html.
documentation_security_justification: Each specification chapter has a Security section that states what users can expect: the permissions it defines and the security context of callbacks (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). OSGi security is optional: without a Java security manager no permission is enforced (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.core/8.0.0/framework.security.html). Supported versions and reporting are in https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md.
documentation_quick_start_justification: The specification chapters contain examples (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/) and the README names the Maven artifact and the compatible implementations, but no quick start guide combines the steps (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md).
documentation_current_justification: The specification text, the Javadoc and the TCK live in this repository and change in the same pull request (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged); README and CONTRIBUTING describe the current Maven build. Released versions stay online at https://docs.osgi.org/specification/. Known defect: the public draft at https://osgi.github.io/osgi/cmpn/ is still built from the former monorepo.
documentation_achievements_justification: The repository front page shows and links the project's achievements: the OpenSSF Scorecard, the CI build status and the Maven Central release (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md). The best practices badge will be added when it is earned.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: N/A: the software is a Java API library without a user interface. The documentation is HTML with headings and alternative text for figures, and is also available as PDF (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
internationalization_justification: N/A: the software is a Java API and generates no text for end users; exception messages are developer diagnostics (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/tree/main/api).
sites_password_security_justification: N/A: the project sites store no user passwords. Source and issues are on GitHub (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log), releases on Maven Central, and https://www.osgi.org and https://docs.osgi.org are pages without their own login; contributors use GitHub and Eclipse Foundation accounts.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The project provides an upgrade path: OSGi semantic versioning keeps minor versions backward compatible (https://docs.osgi.org/whitepaper/semantic-versioning/) and bnd baselining enforces it in every build, so upgrading means changing the dependency version. Security fixes go into the most recent release (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md), and all older specifications stay online (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: N/A: no vulnerability was resolved in the last 12 months (https://www.eclipse.org/security/known/). Under the Eclipse process, credits are a required field of the CVE request (https://csi.eclipse.dev/security-handbook/vulnerabilities/handling.html).
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: The response process is the Eclipse Foundation Security Policy (https://www.eclipse.org/security/policy/), detailed in the Eclipse Project Handbook (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/handbook/#vulnerability): the EF Security Team triages each report, the project security team (all committers, https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/who) fixes it, and a CVE and the disclosure are coordinated. SECURITY.md links the policy (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
coding_standards_justification: The only written style rules are the whitespace rules in https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.editorconfig. CONTRIBUTING.md refers to Eclipse formatter settings that are not in the repository (.settings/ is ignored by git), so no specific Java style guide is identified.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Nothing enforces the style in CI. The parent pom manages the editorconfig-maven-plugin only in pluginManagement, so it never runs (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
build_standard_variables_justification: N/A: the build is Maven and compiles only Java; no native binaries are generated (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/pom.xml).
build_preserve_debug_justification: javac runs with debug information enabled, the default of the maven-compiler-plugin (https://maven.apache.org/plugins/maven-compiler-plugin/compile-mojo.html#debug), and the build does not strip it from the jar (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
build_non_recursive_justification: Maven builds all modules in one reactor and orders them by their declared dependencies (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/pom.xml); there is no recursive build.
build_repeatable_justification: The parent pom fixes project.build.outputTimestamp and runs bnd with -reproducible (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml). Two clean builds of the API and specification jars on 2026-11-19 gave bit-identical files (same SHA-256).
installation_common_justification: The API is installed with the standard package manager of the language: it is on Maven Central as org.osgi:org.osgi.service.log (https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/org.osgi/org.osgi.service.log). The jar is an OSGi bundle and is installed into and removed from a framework through the standard OSGi life-cycle operations.
installation_standard_variables_justific: N/A: there is no installation system that chooses file locations; the artifact is a jar referenced by Maven coordinates (https://docs.osgi.org/artifacts/).
installation_development_quick_justifica: A developer needs JDK 21 and Maven. `mvn clean verify` fetches every dependency, builds everything in the repository and runs the tests and the TCK against a compatible implementation (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md#build, https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
external_dependencies_justification: All external dependencies are declared as Maven coordinates in the pom.xml files (e.g. https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/api/pom.xml); shared versions are managed in the parent pom (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled (https://github.com/osgi/.eclipsefdn/blob/main/otterdog/osgi.jsonnet), weekly version updates are configured (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml), and the OpenSSF Scorecard vulnerability check runs on every push (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/.github/workflows/scorecard-analysis.yml).
updateable_reused_components_justificati: The repository contains no copies of external components. Maven resolves every dependency by coordinate and version, so updating a component is a one-line change that Dependabot automates (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Aapp%2Fdependabot).
interfaces_current_justification: The API uses no deprecated interfaces: a compile with deprecation warnings enabled is clean, and the TCK uses JUnit 5 and AssertJ (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/api/pom.xml). The permission model builds on java.security.Permission, which is not deprecated, although Java 24 no longer enforces permissions (https://openjdk.org/jeps/486).
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push and pull request runs the build workflow (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/actions/workflows/build.yml), which runs the complete TCK in a real OSGi framework against a compatible implementation and publishes the result as a check run (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/spec-build.yml).
regression_tests_added50_justification: Bug fixes come with a regression test in the same pull request, in the TCK or as a unit test (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged; example: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.typedevent/pull/65).
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Coverage is not measured: neither this repository nor the parent pom configures a coverage tool (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
test_policy_mandated_justification: The formal written policy is the Eclipse Foundation Specification Process: every specification version must have a TCK (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/#efsp-tck), and a final specification needs TCK coverage of all verifiable normative statements (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/efsp/operations.php#tck).
implement_secure_design_justification: The specifications apply secure design principles and document them in their Security sections: least privilege through fine-grained permissions, complete mediation through checks by the framework or the service, and validation of names and filters against defined grammars (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). The TCK verifies the specified checks (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: N/A: the project produces Java APIs (interfaces, DTOs, annotations and, where a specification defines them, permission classes), specification texts and TCKs. The API implements and calls no cryptography; implementations provide it where a specification needs it (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
crypto_credential_agility_justification: N/A: the project produces Java APIs (interfaces, DTOs, annotations and, where a specification defines them, permission classes), specification texts and TCKs. The API implements and calls no cryptography; implementations provide it where a specification needs it (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
crypto_used_network_justification: N/A: the released API opens no network connections and uses no TLS. Where a specification describes network communication (for example Remote Services), implementations provide it (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
crypto_tls12_justification: N/A: the released API opens no network connections and uses no TLS. Where a specification describes network communication (for example Remote Services), implementations provide it (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: N/A: the released API opens no network connections and uses no TLS. Where a specification describes network communication (for example Remote Services), implementations provide it (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: N/A: the released API opens no network connections and uses no TLS. Where a specification describes network communication (for example Remote Services), implementations provide it (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/).
signed_releases_justification: Every release on Maven Central has a detached OpenPGP signature (https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/), and the release workflow signs with the project key held by the Eclipse Foundation (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/spec-release.yml). No document tells users how to obtain the public key and verify a download.
version_tags_signed_justification: The repository has no tags yet, and the documented release procedure (the GitHub release form or `gh release create`, https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md#versioning-and-releases) creates unsigned tags.
input_validation_justification: Input from untrusted sources is checked against allowlists: names, topics, filters and versions must match the grammars the specifications define, and invalid input is rejected with defined exceptions (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/). The TCK verifies this (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
hardening_justification: N/A: the released artifact is a Java API jar, memory-safe bytecode without native code, network service or web interface, so compiler, linker and HTTP hardening mechanisms do not apply (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/tree/main/api).
assurance_case_justification: No assurance case exists yet. Its building blocks are the Security sections of the specifications (https://docs.osgi.org/specification/), the organisation security policy (https://github.com/osgi/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md) and the TCK.
achieve_silver_justification: The silver badge is not achieved: the project is not yet registered on https://www.bestpractices.dev/ and several silver criteria in this file are Unmet.
contributors_unassociated_justification: Significant contributions come from unassociated organisations: the history of this repository shows authors from several companies (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/graphs/contributors), the compatible implementations are developed in separate open source projects (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/README.md), and the committers work for different employers (https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/who).
copyright_per_file_justification: Java sources and the specification text carry "Copyright (c) Contributors to the Eclipse Foundation", the form the Eclipse handbook recommends (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/handbook/#ip-copyright-headers); code taken from Apache Felix keeps its ASF header. The Maven and bnd build descriptors, and a few Java files in some repositories, do not carry it yet (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
license_per_file_justification: Java sources and the specification text carry the Apache License 2.0 notice and `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; code taken from Apache Felix keeps its ASF header. The Maven and bnd build descriptors, and a few Java files in some repositories, do not carry it yet (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log).
small_tasks_justification: The repository has the labels "good first issue" and "help wanted", but no issue carries them (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22).
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is enforced for every member of the osgi GitHub organisation, the only way to change the repository: the Eclipse Foundation baseline requires it and its validation rejects organisations without it (https://github.com/EclipseFdn/otterdog-defaults/blob/main/validate-org-settings.py).
secure_2FA_justification: Maintainer to decide. 2FA is enforced, but the method is not restricted and the project has no rule that excludes SMS; the Eclipse security handbook only recommends security keys or TOTP (https://csi.eclipse.dev/security-handbook/developer/account.html#multi-factor-authentication-mfa).
code_review_standards_justification: https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md says that maintainers review and merge pull requests, but not how the review is done, what a reviewer must check or what makes a change acceptable.
two_person_review_justification: Changes reach main through pull requests that a committer other than the author approves (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged); the branch rule of every specification repository requires one approving review (https://github.com/osgi/.eclipsefdn/blob/main/otterdog/osgi.jsonnet).
build_reproducible_justification: The build is reproducible: the parent pom fixes project.build.outputTimestamp and runs bnd with -reproducible (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml). Two clean builds of the API and specification jars on 2026-11-19 gave bit-identical files.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Coverage is not measured: neither this repository nor the parent pom configures a coverage tool (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Coverage is not measured: neither this repository nor the parent pom configures a coverage tool (https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.maven.pom/blob/main/pom.xml).
hardened_site_justification: https://www.osgi.org and https://github.com/osgi/org.osgi.service.log send HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options, but the documentation site https://docs.osgi.org sends no Content-Security-Policy and no X-Frame-Options.
security_review_justification: No security review of the last 5 years is documented. The Eclipse reviews of the project (https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.osgi/governance) check process and intellectual property, not security.
